{{img

===Etymology===
{{ety|en|id=Q5880|:lbor|la:vāgīna<id:sheath><t:sheath>|tree=1|text=+}}

===Pronunciation===
* {{IPA|en|/vəˈdʒaɪ.nə/}}
* {{audio|en|en-us-vagina.ogg|a=US}}
* {{rhymes|en|aɪnə|s=3}}
* {{hyph|en|va|gi|na}}

===Noun===
{{en-noun|+|vaginae|vaginæ<l:archaic>}}

# {{senseid|en|Q5880}} {{lb|en|anatomy}} A [[sex organ]] for [[copulation]] and [[birth]], found in [[female]] [[therian]] [[mammal]]s, consisting of a passage between the [[vulval vestibule]] and the [[cervix]] of the [[uterus]].
#: {{syn|en|Thesaurus:vagina}}
#: {{hyper|en|internal genitalia|;|Müllerian duct|paramesonephric duct|urogenital sinus}}
#* {{quote-book|en|year=1991|author=Richard Evan Jones|title=Human Reproductive Biology|page=61|isbn=9780123897701
|text=The epithelial lining of the '''vagina''' consists of many layers of flattened cells. Changes in the condition of these cells during the menstrual cycle can be detected by swabbing the lining and looking at the cells under a microscope.}}
## {{lb|en|zootomy}} A similar organ in some [[invertebrate]]s and non-mammalian [[amniote]]s.
# {{lb|en|botany}} A [[sheathlike]] structure, such as the [[leaf]] of a [[grass]] that [[surround]]s a [[stem]].
#: {{syn|en|sheath}}
# {{lb|en|colloquial}} The [[vulva]], or the vulva and vaginal passage collectively.
#: {{syn|en|Thesaurus:vulva}}
#* {{see citations|en}}
# {{lb|en|derogatory|colloquial|rare}} A [[coward]]; a [[weakling]]; a [[pussy]].
#* '''2002''', "{{w|The New Terrance And Phillip Movie Trailer}}" (''South Park'' TV episode)
#*: {{quote|en|Don't you interrupt me, you '''vagina'''! I was givin' a heart-wrenchin' soliloquy about me feelin's for Tugger!}}
# {{lb|en|transgender slang|and|gay slang|uncommon}} The [[anus]].

====Usage notes====
* In technical discussions of anatomy, the {{m|en||vagina}} is a wholly internal structure and the {{m|en||vulva}} is wholly external, but in common use (since at least the 1930s)<ref>Besides [[Citations:vagina|these examples from the 1930s onward]], Martha Kirkpatrick, in ''Women’s Sexual Development: Explorations of Inner Space'' (2012), notes that a psychiatrist character played by a real psychiatrist uses ''vagina'' to include the vulva in the 1969 film ''Bob & Carol & Ted & Alice'', and cites another such use from 1970.</ref> the term {{m|en||vagina}} can refer to the {{m|en||vulva}}, or to the vulva and vaginal passage collectively.

====Hypernyms====
* [[Müllerian duct]]s (''upper vagina''), [[urogenital sinus]] (''lower vagina'') - embryological precursors
* {{l|en|internal genitalia}}
